title: Step 1: Get the DOM element
content: In my HTML I create an empty div with an 'id' to access it via JavaScript.

title: Step 2: Creating the Accordion Container
content: I want to emulate the same HTML structure as in the first approach. To do so I create a class AccordionContainer responsible for creating the <dt> with the 'accordion' class.

title: Step 3: Creating the Accordion Section
content: I create a class AccordionSection that generates both <dt> and <dd> with the required attributes. The most important one is the 'aria-expanded' in <dt>, which controls the visibility of the adjacent <dd>.

title: Step 4: Displaying only one section at a time
content: I added a click event to the title that toggles the 'aria-expanded' attribute. To close the previously opened section, I use a static variable to track the last opened element and close it on the next title click.

title: Step 5: Fetching the data
content: I created a .json file to simulate an API response and fetch the data asynchronously.

title: Thank you for your time
content: This concludes my JavaScript exercise. Thank you!
